name: Worx Landroid Vision Cloud WR340
description: Worx's wire-free "Vision Cloud" mower, covering up to 1 acre using stereo-camera V-SLAM navigation and RTK cloud positioning — a separate line from the boundary-wire Landroid M (WR140). Self-explores and vision-maps the yard instead of requiring a perimeter wire.

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: Cloud RTK positioning free for mower's life, per independent review

sourcing: Verified against Worx's own official site and support wiki, a CES 2026 press release (PR Newswire), and independent reviews from Tom's Guide and Reviewed.com. Announced at CES 2026 (January 2026); Best Buy currently lists the WR340 as "Coming Soon," yet Tom's Guide and Reviewed.com had already published hands-on reviews at time of research — likely from early-access review units — so treat broad retail availability as not yet fully confirmed despite press coverage existing. No published noise (dB) rating was found from Worx for this model. Do not confuse this wire-free Vision Cloud line with the separately-catalogued, boundary-wire Landroid M (WR140).

pricing.summary: Best Buy and Tom's Guide independently agree on **$2,299.99** MSRP for the WR340 (1-acre tier). Some pricing shown near the WR340 on worx.com's own site appears to actually belong to the lower-coverage WR310 (~$949–1,199, 1/4 acre) and WR320 (~$1,799, 1/2 acre) siblings in the same Vision Cloud lineup, so don't confuse those figures with the WR340's own price.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: This wire-free mower family (WR310/320/340, tiered by coverage) navigates via stereo camera with V-SLAM and RTK cloud positioning, autonomously mapping the yard without a perimeter wire; the camera also powers Vision AI obstacle detection. Independent testing: Tom's Guide found battery life limiting and slope performance inconsistent above ~20°; Reviewed.com noted debris like sticks can stall the mower.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Some pricing shown near the WR340 on Worx's own website actually belongs to its lower-coverage Vision Cloud siblings rather than the WR340 itself, whose MSRP is $2,299.99 per Best Buy and Tom's Guide. Independent testing from Tom's Guide also found slope performance inconsistent above roughly 20°, despite a spec sheet claiming a 30% (17°) max-slope rating.
